text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Parliament amended the act on customs law and customs proceedings yesterday and passed a bill on protecting art monuments.
- The Constitutional Court ruled yesterday that several aspects of the social insurance law violate the Constitution.
- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny has sent a letter to Health Insurance Authority (EBO) president Laszlo Halmy asking him to consider whether vice president Peter Simsa is competent for his post.
- Pope John Paul II will receive Prime Minister Gyula Horn at a private audience June 20 after Horn signs an agreement between the Holy See and Hungary on financing the Catholic Church in Hungary.
- 46 Hungarian soldiers had flown to the United States to take part in the Cooperative Nugget '97 war games in Louisiana.
- Industrial production rose 9% in April compared to March and 11.4% from a year earlier.
- Whatever the outcome of the 1998 elections will be, the current economic policy will prevail, Prime Minister Gyula Horn told an investment summit in Budapest yesterday.
- Tenders pertaining to two national commercial radio networks were made public Tuesday.
- Oil and gas company MOL is exerting great pressure on the Hungarian Energy Office (MEH) for a large energy price hike when the MEH decides on the matter next month.
- A 45% percent stake in dairy company Szabolcstej will be offered in exchange for compensation coupons holders on June 23, the first in a new series of share issues for coupon holders.
- Postabank Rt. will hold an extraordinary general meeting on July 11.
- The Generali insurance company will soon sell most of its 74% stake in Europai Utazasi Biztosito Rt.

- Fifth district administrative chief Judit Xantus, backed up by five policemen, sealed the Mephisto club on Vaci utca and the nearby Fontana nightclub on Regiposta utca Tuesday in the latest clampdowns on catering spots that have recently overcharged foreigners.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The Mint has begun printing notes in the new denominations of Ft 200, Ft 2,000 and Ft 10,000.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The economic boom became more tangible in the first quarter, according to the Central Statistics Office data.
- The government has increased its GDP growth projections by 0.5 percent to 8,050 billion forints and the wage outflow from 16-17 percent to 21 percent this year.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Parliament's constitutional committee will today hear the nominees for the vacant Constitutional Court posts.
